items.title: Anaesthesia & Operation Theatre Technology
items.summary: For B.Sc. and diploma students in anaesthesia and OT technology, and for working technologists who want to sharpen their basics.
items.audience: B.Sc. / diploma AOTT students and working OT & anaesthesia technologists
items.overview:
A structured course that follows the NCAHP curriculum for Anaesthesia & Operation Theatre Technology. Each topic is taught live, with time for questions, case discussions and practical tips from the operating room.
- Small groups, so you can ask questions
- Notes after every class
- Regular quizzes and viva practice
items.modules:
Basics of anatomy & physiology for the OT: airway, respiratory and cardiovascular systems
Pharmacology for anaesthesia technologists: induction agents, inhalational agents, opioids, muscle relaxants and reversal
The anaesthesia workstation: gas supply, cylinders and pin index, vaporisers, breathing circuits and machine checks
Airway management: assessment, airway devices, intubation assistance and the difficult airway cart
Patient monitoring: ECG, NIBP, SpO2, capnography, temperature and alarms
Regional anaesthesia: spinal, epidural and nerve blocks, and how to assist safely
OT design, sterilisation and infection control: CSSD, autoclave cycles, asepsis and waste handling
Patient preparation and positioning: pre-op checks, WHO surgical safety checklist and safe positioning
Emergencies in the OT: BLS/ACLS basics, malignant hyperthermia, anaphylaxis and the crash cart
Recovery room (PACU) care and post-operative monitoring
Anaesthesia for specialities: obstetrics, paediatrics, cardiac, neuro and day care
Clinical case discussions, viva and practical exam practice
items.outcomes:
Check and prepare an anaesthesia machine and breathing circuit
Assist confidently with airway management and intubation
Read and respond to OT monitoring and alarms
Apply sterilisation and infection-control standards in the OT
Respond to common OT emergencies as part of the team
Answer viva and interview questions with confidence

items.title: Critical Care Technology
items.summary: For B.Sc. and diploma students in critical care technology, and ICU technologists who want stronger basics in ventilation, monitoring and ICU equipment.
items.audience: B.Sc. / diploma Critical Care Technology students and working ICU technologists
items.overview:
A course that follows the NCAHP curriculum for Critical Care Technology. Each topic is taught live with ICU cases, equipment walkthroughs and time for questions.
- Small groups, so you can ask questions
- Notes after every class
- Regular quizzes and viva practice
items.modules:
Applied anatomy & physiology for the ICU: respiratory, cardiovascular, renal and nervous systems
Pharmacology in critical care: sedatives, analgesics, vasopressors, inotropes and infusion calculations
Oxygen therapy and airway care: oxygen devices, humidification, suctioning and tracheostomy care
Mechanical ventilation: modes, settings, alarms, weaning and ventilator-associated complications
Non-invasive ventilation and high-flow nasal oxygen: interfaces, set-up and monitoring
Haemodynamic monitoring: ECG, invasive arterial and central venous pressure, transducer set-up and zeroing
Arterial blood gas analysis: sampling, the analyser and interpretation of acid–base disorders
ICU equipment care: ventilators, monitors, infusion and syringe pumps, defibrillators and calibration
Infection control in the ICU: hand hygiene, isolation, bundle care (VAP, CLABSI, CAUTI) and biomedical waste
Resuscitation and emergencies: BLS/ACLS, crash cart, shock, sepsis and cardiac arrest teamwork
Renal and neuro critical care basics: CRRT overview, fluid balance, GCS and neuro monitoring
Clinical case discussions, viva and practical exam practice
items.outcomes:
Set up, check and troubleshoot an ICU ventilator
Recognise and respond to ventilator and monitor alarms
Set up invasive pressure monitoring and zero a transducer
Collect and interpret an arterial blood gas sample
Apply ICU infection-control bundles
Answer viva and interview questions with confidence

items.title: Cardiac Care Technology
items.summary: For B.Sc. and diploma students in cardiac care technology who want clear teaching on ECG, echo, cath lab and cardiac investigations.
items.audience: B.Sc. / diploma Cardiac Care Technology students and working cardiac technologists
items.overview:
A course that follows the NCAHP curriculum for Cardiac Care Technology, covering non-invasive tests, the cath lab and cardiac emergencies, with tracings and case examples in every class.
- Small groups, so you can ask questions
- Notes after every class
- Regular quizzes and viva practice
items.modules:
Anatomy & physiology of the heart: chambers, valves, coronary circulation and conduction system
Cardiac pharmacology: antiplatelets, anticoagulants, anti-arrhythmics, nitrates and emergency drugs
ECG recording and interpretation: lead placement, rhythm, axis, blocks, ischaemia and infarction
Arrhythmias: recognition and first response to tachy- and bradyarrhythmias
Holter monitoring and ambulatory blood pressure monitoring
Treadmill test (TMT): protocols, patient preparation, monitoring and safety
Echocardiography basics: views, M-mode, 2D, Doppler and common findings
Cath lab: set-up, radiation safety, angiography, angioplasty and haemodynamic recording
Pacemakers and devices: temporary and permanent pacing, ICDs and basic checks
Cardiac emergencies: ACS, cardiac arrest, defibrillation, cardioversion and the crash cart
Infection control, patient safety and documentation in cardiac units
Clinical case discussions, viva and practical exam practice
items.outcomes:
Record a good-quality 12-lead ECG and recognise common abnormalities
Prepare a patient for and assist with a treadmill test
Explain standard echo views and common findings
Prepare the cath lab and follow radiation safety
Respond to cardiac emergencies as part of the team
Answer viva and interview questions with confidence

items.title: Dialysis Therapy Technology
items.summary: For B.Sc. and diploma students in dialysis therapy technology, and dialysis technicians who want stronger basics in machines, water treatment and patient care.
items.audience: B.Sc. / diploma Dialysis Therapy Technology students and working dialysis technicians
items.overview:
A course that follows the NCAHP curriculum for Dialysis Therapy Technology, with machine walkthroughs, water-treatment basics and patient-care cases in every class.
- Small groups, so you can ask questions
- Notes after every class
- Regular quizzes and viva practice
items.modules:
Renal anatomy & physiology: nephron, filtration, fluid and electrolyte balance
Kidney disease: acute kidney injury, chronic kidney disease, stages and indications for dialysis
Principles of dialysis: diffusion, ultrafiltration, convection and dialyser types
The haemodialysis machine: circuits, alarms, priming, disinfection and troubleshooting
Water treatment for dialysis: RO plant, monitoring, testing and quality standards
Vascular access: AV fistula, grafts and catheters, cannulation and access care
Running a dialysis session: patient assessment, prescription, monitoring and documentation
Anticoagulation in dialysis: heparin, heparin-free dialysis and monitoring
Complications during dialysis: hypotension, cramps, air embolism and their management
Peritoneal dialysis and CRRT: principles, set-up and patient care
Infection control in the dialysis unit: hepatitis B/C and HIV precautions, reprocessing of dialysers
Clinical case discussions, viva and practical exam practice
items.outcomes:
Prime, run and troubleshoot a haemodialysis machine
Understand RO water treatment and its quality checks
Cannulate and care for vascular access safely
Recognise and respond to complications during dialysis
Follow infection-control and reprocessing standards
Answer viva and interview questions with confidence

items.title: Medical Laboratory Sciences
items.summary: For B.Sc. and diploma students in medical laboratory sciences who want clear, practical teaching across the core lab disciplines.
items.audience: B.Sc. / diploma MLT students and working laboratory technologists
items.overview:
A course that follows the NCAHP curriculum for Medical Laboratory Sciences, covering haematology, biochemistry, microbiology, pathology and quality, with practical examples from real labs.
- Small groups, so you can ask questions
- Notes after every class
- Regular quizzes and viva practice
items.modules:
Laboratory basics: equipment, glassware, safety, and specimen collection and handling
Haematology: blood counts, peripheral smear, ESR and haemoglobin estimation
Coagulation studies: PT/INR, aPTT, bleeding and clotting time
Clinical biochemistry: glucose, renal and liver function tests, lipids and electrolytes
Automation in the lab: analysers, calibration and troubleshooting
Microbiology: staining, culture media, sterilisation and antibiotic sensitivity testing
Serology and immunology: ELISA, rapid tests and antigen–antibody reactions
Blood bank and transfusion: grouping, cross-matching, component separation and safety
Histopathology and cytology: tissue processing, sectioning, staining and PAP smears
Clinical pathology: urine, stool and body-fluid analysis
Quality control and NABL standards: internal QC, Levey–Jennings charts and documentation
Practical case discussions, viva and exam practice
items.outcomes:
Collect, label and handle specimens correctly
Perform and verify routine haematology and biochemistry tests
Prepare and read Gram stains and set up cultures
Perform blood grouping and cross-matching safely
Apply quality control and NABL documentation
Answer viva and interview questions with confidence

items.title: Radiology & Imaging Technology
items.summary: For B.Sc. and diploma students in radiology and imaging technology who want strong basics in radiography, CT, MRI and radiation safety.
items.audience: B.Sc. / diploma Radiology & Imaging Technology students and working radiographers
items.overview:
A course that follows the NCAHP curriculum for Radiology & Imaging Technology, with positioning walkthroughs, image examples and safety practice in every class.
- Small groups, so you can ask questions
- Notes after every class
- Regular quizzes and viva practice
items.modules:
Radiographic anatomy: skeletal, chest and abdominal anatomy for imaging
Radiation physics: X-ray production, interactions with matter and image formation
Radiation protection: ALARA, dosimetry, shielding and AERB guidelines
Radiographic equipment: X-ray tubes, generators, digital radiography and CR/DR systems
Radiographic positioning: chest, skull, spine and limbs
Contrast media and special procedures: IVU, barium studies, HSG and reaction management
Computed tomography (CT): principles, protocols, contrast and patient preparation
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI): principles, safety screening and common sequences
Ultrasound basics: principles, probes and assisting in scans
Mammography, fluoroscopy and portable radiography
Image quality, PACS and digital image management
Practical case discussions, viva and exam practice
items.outcomes:
Position patients correctly for routine radiographs
Apply radiation-protection principles and AERB rules
Explain the principles of CT and MRI and prepare patients safely
Recognise and respond to contrast reactions
Judge image quality and manage images in PACS
Answer viva and interview questions with confidence

items.title: Emergency & Trauma Care
items.summary: For B.Sc. and diploma students in emergency and trauma care technology who want confident, practical teaching for the emergency department.
items.audience: B.Sc. / diploma Emergency & Trauma Care students and working ED technologists
items.overview:
A course that follows the NCAHP curriculum for Emergency & Trauma Care Technology, built around scenarios, triage practice and step-by-step emergency procedures.
- Small groups, so you can ask questions
- Notes after every class
- Regular quizzes and viva practice
items.modules:
Applied anatomy & physiology for emergencies
Triage: principles, triage systems and documentation
Basic and advanced life support: BLS, ACLS and paediatric life support
Airway and breathing emergencies: airway adjuncts, bag-mask ventilation and oxygen therapy
Trauma care: primary and secondary survey, ATLS principles and spinal immobilisation
Shock and haemorrhage control: types of shock, IV access and fluid resuscitation
Cardiac emergencies: chest pain pathway, arrhythmias and defibrillation
Medical emergencies: stroke, seizures, diabetic emergencies, poisoning and snakebite
Burns, wounds and fractures: assessment, dressing, splinting and first aid
Emergency equipment and drugs: crash cart, monitors, defibrillator and emergency drug doses
Disaster management, mass-casualty incidents and pre-hospital care
Simulation scenarios, viva and practical exam practice
items.outcomes:
Triage patients and document correctly
Perform high-quality BLS and assist in ACLS
Carry out a primary trauma survey and immobilise the spine
Manage airway and breathing emergencies with basic adjuncts
Prepare and check the crash cart and emergency equipment
Answer viva and interview questions with confidence

items.title: Respiratory Therapy
items.summary: For B.Sc. and diploma students in respiratory therapy who want clear teaching on lung function, oxygen therapy, ventilation and pulmonary care.
items.audience: B.Sc. / diploma Respiratory Therapy students and working respiratory therapists
items.overview:
A course that follows the NCAHP curriculum for Respiratory Therapy, with equipment walkthroughs, ventilator cases and breathing-care techniques in every class.
- Small groups, so you can ask questions
- Notes after every class
- Regular quizzes and viva practice
items.modules:
Respiratory anatomy & physiology: mechanics of breathing, gas exchange and control of breathing
Respiratory pharmacology: bronchodilators, steroids, mucolytics and inhaler technique
Pulmonary function testing: spirometry, peak flow and interpretation
Arterial blood gases: sampling and interpretation
Oxygen therapy: devices, humidification, high-flow systems and oxygen toxicity
Aerosol therapy and airway clearance: nebulisers, chest physiotherapy and suctioning
Airway management: artificial airways, tracheostomy care and intubation assistance
Mechanical ventilation: modes, settings, graphics, alarms and weaning
Non-invasive ventilation: CPAP, BiPAP, interfaces and monitoring
Neonatal and paediatric respiratory care basics
Pulmonary rehabilitation, sleep studies and home respiratory care
Clinical case discussions, viva and practical exam practice
items.outcomes:
Perform and interpret spirometry
Choose and set up the right oxygen and aerosol devices
Interpret arterial blood gases
Set up and adjust ventilators and NIV safely
Teach correct inhaler technique and airway clearance
Answer viva and interview questions with confidence
